newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukrainian currency seen convertible next year.
newsitem.headline: Ukrainian currency seen convertible next year.

text.p: Ukraine's new hryvnia currency should become convertible next year, President Leonid Kuchma's top economic adviser said.

Valery Lytvytsky told Reuters that 1997 budget forecasts of 24.9 percent annual inflation and 1.7 percent growth in gross domestic product should enable the hryvnia, introduced on September 2, to be fully convertible by next year.
The old karbovanets currency was withdrawn from circulation on Monday, September 16.
"It's not right to say that currency reform in Ukraine ended on September 16 with the changeover to the hryvnia," Valery Lytvytsky told Reuters.
"It is our goal to make the hryvnia fully convertible against Western currencies by the end of next year."
